[{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Bachelor of Science Major in Biochemistry with Departmental Honors","groupId":"cfbc6127-8e20-404d-a50e-0194a98d54db","position":0,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Students must complete a minimum of 120 credits with a Pacific cumulative and major/program grade point average of 2.0 in order to earn the Bachelor of Science degree with a major in biochemistry.

","groupId":"0369b72c-0a1c-4c1a-b88e-0194a98d54dc","position":1,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"General Education Requirements","groupId":"0a520c2d-1ea4-4a24-bb24-0194a98e616f","position":2,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

For more details, see General Education

Minimum 28 units and 9 courses that include:

","groupId":"ca92c091-6d55-408c-8ca8-0194a98e616f","position":3,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"CORE Seminars (2 courses)","groupId":"4bad8a7a-6e69-413a-939b-0194a98e616f","position":4,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Notes:

1) CORE Seminars cannot be taken for Pass/No Credit. 

2) Transfer students with 28 or more transfer credits taken after high school are exempt from both CORE seminars.  

","groupId":"29b8b3db-62e8-4ce7-a6a8-0194a98e616f","position":5,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Breadth Requirement (7 courses, at least 3 units each)","groupId":"19cff724-6d40-4568-b6f4-0194a98e616f","position":6,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Notes:

1) No more than 2 courses from a single discipline can be used to meet the Breadth Requirement.

2) The student must complete 60 units outside the primary discipline of the first major, regardless of the department who offers the course(s) in that discipline. (This includes general education courses, transfer courses, CPCE/EXTN units, internships, etc.)

","groupId":"25a5bb94-ac0b-4c4e-b77a-0194a98e616f","position":7,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Diversity and Inclusion Requirement","groupId":"f9869ede-c39c-46e5-a5c4-0194a98f1122","position":8,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

All students must complete Diversity and Inclusion coursework (at least 3 units)

Note: Diversity and Inclusion courses can also be used to meet the breadth category requirements, or major or minor requirements.

","groupId":"e406a4ca-dd6f-4844-9512-0194a98f1123","position":9,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Fundamental Skills","groupId":"e1696388-e95e-4e06-b7a0-0194a98f1123","position":10,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Students must demonstrate competence in:

Writing

Quantitative Analysis (Math)

Note: Failure to satisfy the fundamental skills requirements by the end of four semesters of full-time study at the University is grounds for academic disqualification.

","groupId":"5c34af29-6251-4346-a068-0194a98f1123","position":11,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralTitle","content":"Major Requirements","groupId":"4c726538-696c-4cfa-90bd-0194a98f65f3","position":12,"area":"General"},{"type":"GeneralText","content":"

Notes:

﻿1)At least 4 of your major required courses must be taken at Pacific.

2) Students are strongly recommended to engage in undergraduate research as an elective.

3) In addition, students are encouraged to complete at least one other course in biology and at least one semester of research.

4) Section 4 and 5 are two different tracks namely Conventional Track and ACS Accredited Track and the choice of any one of them is required.

5) Students must complete at least two semesters of CHEM 197. A written research thesis must be submitted, which will be read by the academic advisor and one other Chemistry faculty member. The thesis must be presented to the Department and defended.
